newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLO/Bund spread would test 8 bps but for auction.
newsitem.headline: OLO/Bund spread would test 8 bps but for auction.

text.p: Only the prospect of new supply held back Belgian 10-year linear bonds (OLOs) on Tuesday from trading through the record low eight basis point yield spread over Bunds set on Friday, dealers said.
Once today's Treasury exchange auction was out of the way a move towards a spread of five basis points in the 10-year area was likely, they said.

"In Belgium everything stays pretty well bid, especially in the four to seven year area," one trader at a foreign primary dealer said. "As long as these (maturities) stay solid the 10-year spread can come down."
OLO dealers said the market remained unmoved by weakness in neighbouring Germany. A domestic primary dealer said Germany was "taking profits in a bull run."
As usual, the Belgian market tended to outperform rather than underperform Germany, he said.
The benchmark May 2006 OLO yielded 6.11 percent at around 0845 GMT, unchanged from a day earlier, but the spread narrowed to nine from 10 basis points.
"If the Bund turns higher then we could widen again a bit, but at the moment its only the auction which is stopping us from going higher," he added.
